title: A migration revision that declares itself expand-only holds only expand operations
intent: A revision may declare that the previous release keeps working on the schema it leaves. That promise is what lets a release be rolled back by starting the previous release again on the same database, instead of restoring a backup and losing every write made since. It holds only for a closed list of operations: creating a table together with what is its own (its keys, constraints and indexes, unique ones included, a foreign key from it only with a cascading or nulling delete action and never onto a table whose rows are soft-deleted rather than deleted) and seeding the rows of that new table; adding a column to an existing table that is nullable, has a default or is generated, and declares no uniqueness, no check and at most a nulling foreign key on that nullable column; and adding an index that is not unique. Everything else breaks it: any drop, rename, type change or tightening; a uniqueness or check constraint, a unique index or a primary key change on an existing table; any raw statement or data write to an existing table; rebuilding a table; and a revision that merges two branches. A declaration the operations do not support is refused before the release ships, and refused again while the migration runs, before the operation executes. There is no opt-out: a revision that needs an operation off the list declares that it is not expand-only, which costs only the restore-free rollback of its own release.
reference: A revision file whose module level declares expand_only = True is read; terp migrate make always writes expand_only = False, and adds a comment where every operation it generated is on the list, so the author raises the mark. In upgrade(): create_table (a ForeignKey or ForeignKeyConstraint from it with ondelete CASCADE or SET NULL, onto no table whose model composes SoftDeleteMixin), add_column whose inline Column is nullable, carries a server_default or is Computed, and declares no unique, no CheckConstraint and no ForeignKey but a SET NULL one on a nullable column, create_foreign_key over columns the same revision added nullable with ondelete SET NULL, create_index that is not unique, add_column, create_index, create_unique_constraint, create_check_constraint, create_primary_key and bulk_insert on a table the same revision creates, and a batch_alter_table block (never recreate='always') of such operations, are on the list. Every other Alembic operation, execute(), get_bind(), a merge revision (a tuple down_revision) and a mark that is not a literal bool are flagged, one finding per line. No marker suppresses a finding, and a no_destructive_migrations marker excuses nothing here.

runtime.rationale: The Terp-owned migration environment wraps each revision's upgrade(), so for a revision marked expand-only it knows where the step starts: each operation is classified as Alembic dispatches it, and one off the list raises before its DDL runs online or is written offline (terp migrate upgrade --sql exits non-zero naming it); any other statement the revision sends outside an admitted operation is refused before it runs, op.get_bind() included in both modes; and online on PostgreSQL the catalogue the step left is compared, inside the step's transaction after its version update, with the one it started from, which is how a batch block that rebuilt its table is judged. The checks run in the revision's own process, so they catch mistakes, not a hostile revision; the backup taken before every migration run is the defence against that.
